title: Food, Drinks and Quantities
introduction: Ask for food and describe amounts in familiar situations.
definition: Ask for food and describe amounts in familiar situations.
rules: Use some with amounts that are not specified.
Use a or an with one countable item.

examples.question: May I have ___ milk? (some or an)
steps: Milk is uncountable in this use.

examples.question: I want ___ apple. (a or an)
steps: Apple starts with a vowel sound.

exercises.question: May I have ___ milk? (some or an)
exercises.solution: Milk is uncountable in this use.

exercises.question: I want ___ apple. (a or an)
exercises.solution: Apple starts with a vowel sound.

exercises.question: Two ___ of water. (glass or glasses)
exercises.solution: Use the plural glasses after two.

exercises.question: Which is a vegetable: cucumber or bread?
exercises.solution: Cucumber is commonly used as a vegetable in meals.

exercises.question: Complete: a bowl ___ soup.
exercises.solution: Use of to connect a container and its contents.

exercises.question: Complete: I would like a ___. (sandwich or rice)

summary: Ask for food and describe amounts in familiar situations. Use some with amounts that are not specified.
